primary_topics: Address about Fr. Michael Nolan and the Student Catholic Action (SCA) as the instruments that introduced CJP to Christ -- citing his own Valedictory Address of December 6, 2006 where he publicly paid tribute to Fr. Nolan
The secular upbringing: born Catholic but raised without faith; parents not steeped in their own faith; public school education; UST Trinity failure; FEU as the turning point

Fr. Nolan's specific contributions: built the FEU chapel; recruited CJP to Student Catholic Action; taught him the rudiments of Catholicism; supported his extra-curricular activities; encouraged NUSP formation; helped bring elite Catholic schools into NUSP
The canonical arc: from Catholic ignoramus (didn't know the Holy Trinity) to Pontifical Council for the Laity member at the Vatican -- 'a pure gift from the Almighty'
sub_topics: Valedictory Address citation: 'Towering above them are Fr. Michael Nolan, now in the Great Beyond, who, as chaplain of Far Eastern University and as archdiocesan director of the Student Catholic Action in the 1950s, introduced me to our Lord; to Fr. James Sheehy, his successor, who eventually baptized all of my five children'
The need for explanation: 'That I credited Fr. Nolan and SCA with introducing me to our Lord Jesus Christ at a late stage in my life when I was already in college needs some explanation'
Born poor, purely secular education: public schools; no faith at home; parents not steeped in faith; times were tough after WWII; child labor in Sampaloc; 'there was no faith to comfort me'
UST Trinity failure: the three questions; 'Jesus, Mary, Joseph' answer; 'I failed the test miserably. Disheartened, I enrolled at FEU.'

FEU as the spiritual turning point: 'While FEU prided itself in being nonsectarian, it was during my FEU days when I met persons who, little by little, initially fed my soul that was in search of faith and of my God'
Fr. Nolan: under whose watch the FEU chapel was built; recruited CJP into Student Catholic Action; taught rudiments of Catholicism; 'took a personal interest in me and in what I did'
Fr. James Sheehy: another Columban priest; 'insisted that a good Catholic must not only be personally pure, but must also lead others to purity; in short, be a Christ to others'

NUSP and the Catholic schools: Fr. Nolan helped CJP convince Ateneo, La Salle, Maryknoll, Holy Spirit, St. Scholastica's, UST, University of San Carlos, University of San Agustin and others to join NUSP; 'FEU, under my leadership, bolted the then existing national student organizations which were suspected to be communist fronts'

The communism shield: 'I was most fortunate that when I was elected President of the FEU Central Student Organization, Fr. Nolan was already my spiritual adviser. Otherwise, given my reformist streak, I could have joined the extremist groups' led by Jose Ma. Sison and Satur Ocampo

Meeting Leni: through NUSP; St. Scholastica's College represented by 'a lovely, sweet, thoughtful and intelligent lady, Ms Elenita A. Carpio, who after a fabled courtship agreed to be my wife and lifelong partner'
BLD and deeper faith: mid-1980s; Bukas Loob sa Diyos; read over 100 books on Bible and Catholicism; Second Plenary Council (1991); Pontifical Council for the Laity (Vatican, 1996-2000)

The arc completed: 'this ignorant poor boy who did not even know the three persons of the Holy Trinity became an adviser of the Holy Father as a member of the Pontifical Council for the Laity based in the Vatican. I consider this a pure gift from the Almighty'

stances.claim: Fr. Nolan's most consequential act was not just introducing CJP to the Catholic faith but also serving as a spiritual adviser during the period when CJP was most vulnerable to being recruited by communist student organizations led by Jose Ma. Sison and Satur Ocampo. 'I was most fortunate... Fr. Nolan was already my spiritual adviser. Otherwise, given my reformist streak, I could have joined the extremist groups.' one_paragraph_summary: Published October 20, 2011, this address by CJP elaborates on his Valedictory Address of December 6, 2006 where he paid tribute to Fr. Michael Nolan ('now in the Great Beyond') as the FEU chaplain and archdiocesan director of the Student Catholic Action who 'introduced me to our Lord,' and to Fr. James Sheehy (his Columban successor who baptized all five Panganiban children). The explanation requires his full secular-upbringing narrative: born Catholic but raised without faith (parents not steeped in their own); public schools; no faith to comfort him during the child-labor years; UST Trinity failure ('Jesus, Mary, Joseph'); enrolled at FEU 'no questions asked.' At FEU, Fr. Nolan -- under whose watch the FEU Chapel was built -- 'took a personal interest in me and in what I did,' recruited him into the Student Catholic Action and taught him the rudiments of Catholicism. Fr. Sheehy added: 'a good Catholic must not only be personally pure, but must also lead others to purity; in short, be a Christ to others.' Fr. Nolan supported CJP's student leadership, helping him become the youngest and first sophomore FEU CSO President, then egging him on to organize NUSP -- and crucially, helping him convince elite Catholic schools (Ateneo, La Salle, Maryknoll, Holy Spirit, St. Scholastica's, UST, San Carlos, San Agustin) to leave their 'sheltered cocoons' and join NUSP ('FEU bolted the then existing national student organizations which were suspected to be communist fronts'). The most consequential protection: 'I was most fortunate that when I was elected FEU CSO President, Fr. Nolan was already my spiritual adviser. Otherwise, given my reformist streak, I could have joined the extremist groups' led by Jose Ma. Sison and Satur Ocampo. Through NUSP, CJP met Leni Carpio (St. Scholastica's; 'a fabled courtship'). Later: Bukas Loob sa Diyos (mid-1980s), Second Plenary Council (1991), Pontifical Council for the Laity (Vatican, 1996-2000). The arc: 'this ignorant poor boy who did not even know the three persons of the Holy Trinity became an adviser of the Holy Father. I consider this a pure gift from the Almighty.'
